Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has confirmed he backs an energy ceasefire with Russia, which was announced by US President Donald Trump.
 
Zelensky says he is “awaiting details from the American side”, while Russia and Vladimir Putin are yet to comment.
 
The energy ceasefire was first announced in a post by Trump, after his previous calls for Ukraine to stop attacking Russian oil refineries.

author: BBC News
description:
US President Donald Trump has said he thinks "it's time for Ukraine to get a new president" as he responded to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky's criticism of the US diesel deal with Russia.

Under the deal, Russia would release an initial 300,000 tonnes of diesel "to the American and global marketplace" followed by an additional 500,000 tonnes in November.

We look at what’s behind Trump getting closer to Russia and its President, Vladimir Putin, as well as why he’s again turned against Zelensky.

And they discuss a suspected Houthi attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia in which at least 12 people were killed and 309 injured.

description:
Built in 1886, the Kaiser Friedrich started life as a steam ship, carrying nearly 300 passengers through Berlin's winding rivers and canals every day. 
 
Years later, it was renamed “Siegfried", a title it kept for some time before returning to its original name. 
 
Tech Now's Andrew Rogers took a trip on this historic ship, which has now been converted from steam-powered to electric to ensure it is fit for the future.

Tech Now's Paul Carter finds out how technology powering advanced prosthetics is also helping train humanoid robots.

One is to give somebody their grip back. The other is to take what that person's hand already knows - and teach it to a machine.

description:
How can you spend years paying off your student loan and still owe more than you borrowed? 

Ten years ago, the first Plan 2 borrowers started repaying their student loans. Since then, graduates who left university with similar debts have found themselves on very different financial paths. 

The amount you earn affects how much you repay, how much interest builds up and whether you'll ever clear your balance. BBC Education Correspondent Hazel Shearing investigates why so many graduates are frustrated with the system and what their student loan really means for their future.

author: BBC News
description:
Yemen's Houthis have warned aviation firms and passengers against using Saudi airports and airspace, after 12 people were killed in an attack on the international airport in Riyadh.

More than 300 were injured in Saturday's attack on King Khalid International Airport in Saudi Arabia.

The Houthi statement on Sunday did not directly refer to Saturday's attack, but previously did say they were behind separate strikes on the same airport on Thursday.

Four Saudis, two people from Bangladesh and one person each from the US, Jordan, Palestine, Syria, Sudan and Egypt were killed, the Saudi civil aviation authority said.

author: BBC News
description:
In this episode, we look at critical voices from within Green leader Zack Polanski’s own party, plus calls for a rule change on how the party decides policy.

Last week a motion that declared Zionism a form of racism was voted on and became policy.

Debate over the motion and it’s fallout dominated a week in which he may have preferred to have been focussing on campaigning in Holborn and St Pancras, where he came second to Labour in a by-election.

It means Andy Burnham’s first electoral victory as PM was in London. We use that fact as an excuse to look at his relationship with the capital, and the politics of it. London Centric’s Jim Waterson joins Victoria and Paddy for that.

Subscribe to our channel here: https://bbc.in/bbcnews
